newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STOCK MARKET CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: Concerns about possible big losses on U.S. markets on Friday after stronger-than-expected job creation data spooked South African industrial stocks which, although ending firm, slid well off earlier highs.
Gold stocks finished strong for the first time in seven sessions as bullion steamed, and held, above the $358 level after sinking to below $354, its weakest level in 3-1/4 years, earlier in the week.
"Stocks reversed some of their gains on the U.S. employment figures, as people now anticipate the Dow opening lower," a trader said.
U.S. government figures showed the country added 262,000 new jobs in December, far above the consensus estimate of 192,000, fuelling fears of higher inflation and interest rates.

Local dealers said hefty falls on the Dow on Friday would weigh on South African stocks on Monday as the market had lately again begun to track the U.S. after going its separate way for much of last year.
However, local factors continued to nurture positive sentiment in the market.
"Bonds were strong today and the rand was also firmer for part of it although ending weaker," a dealer said, adding that there was some good natural demand both local and abroad for stocks.
"I have seen over the past few days the natural building up of people wanting to buy stock," he said.
Industrial shares opened strong following a 76-point gain on Wall Street on Thursday. The index touched a best level of 8,088.1 -- a rise of almost 70 points.

At the close the industrial index was up 19.2 points at 8,039.3. Amongst shares SA Breweries climbed 150 cents to 121.75 rand, Remgro lifted 90 cents to 42.90 rand, Barlows jumped 155 cents to 45.30 rand but Amic ditched 150 cents to 166 rand.
On the gold board, stocks ended firmer for the first time this year, finishing the day more than two percent or 31.7 points firmer at 1,421.8.
Traders said interest had returned to gold stocks, but that they remained cautious in the light of bullion's recent volatile moves.
"Golds should be steady to firmer next week, depending on what the gold price does," a dealer said.
Amongst shares Vaal Reefs was up 13 rand at 295 rand, Freegold gained 80 cents to 33 rand and Dries lifted 50 cents to 45 rand.
Dealers said activity on the bourse had returned to normal levels after a quiet Christmas and early new year period with shares worth 683 million rand trading on Friday.
They said volumes were boosted by a few large deals, notably a 50 million rand corporate finance deal, suspected of being part of an asset swap, in Impala Platinum.
Over a million Impala shares traded with the price ending up 100 cents at 49.50 rand. Big trades were also seen in Persetel and Plessey, dealers said.

On the equity futures market industrial and all-share contracts, which began the day firm on Wall Street's strong Thursday gains, slid in later trade amid worries about losses on the U.S. market on Friday.
Gold contracts lifted slightly as bullion remained stable at firmer levels.
The March all-share contract was at 6,170/85 from 6,198, the industrial index contract was at 7,875/85 from 7,893 and the gold index contract was at 1,002/10 from 993.
-- Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
